START metric calculation for a given category Results The proposed methods presented above give us the ability to assess and rank the importance of pre-defined topics within a corpus of text. By applying these methods to both academic and trade literature corpora, we can define the differences between the ways that these bodies of literature understand and address salient topics within the field of MDHD EV adoption. These results present comparative results in terms of saliency (derived from LDA) c-TF-IDF (derived from BERTopic), and the START metric to inform discussion of these comparisons. Saliency Results from LDA Figure 36 shows a comparison of category saliency from both the academic and industry corpora. Each saliency metric is presented with error bars that represent the sample variance resulting from the 100 computational experiments. As illustrated in Figure 36, within the academic corpus, the topics of long-term cost, suitability, short term cost, driver acceptance and brand image all hold an equal saliency. The industry corpus holds long-term cost, suitability, and short- term cost as highly salient, but reduces reliability and familiarity to an intermediate importance before ranking the other categories as a shared bottom-level priority. We also see that familiarity, suitability/compatibility, and sustainability are the only categories that score higher in the industry corpus than in the academic corpus, on average, considering the displayed error. Further, brand image, driver acceptance, long-term cost, reliability, and short-term cost are all significant higher, on average, for academic than for industry (error bars don’t overlap). 85 Bradley, T.H., et al., Agent-Based, Bottom-Up Medium- and Heavy-duty Electric Vehicle Economics, Operation, Charging and Adoption, Final Technical Report, DE-EE0009664 Figure 36. Average normalized saliency. Sample variance is displayed with error bars. C-TF-IDF Results from BERTopic Figure 37 compares the c-TF-IDF scores from the academic and industry corpora using normalized topic saliency. The absence of error bars in this figure is because the synonym mapping step does not occur when using BERTopic [13]. Using the tokenized sentences from each corpus and referencing them against the original BERTopic training data outlined in section 0, we see that the two corpora agree on product familiarity as the most important category. The category of suitability/compatibility, the most salient category from LDA, is ranked more evenly with reliability for the two corpora. Sustainability and brand image are higher for industry than for the academic corpus. Driver acceptance, long-term cost, norms, policy are all higher for the academic corpus than for the industry corpus. 86 Bradley, T.H., et al., Agent-Based, Bottom-Up Medium- and Heavy-duty Electric Vehicle Economics, Operation, Charging and Adoption, Final Technical Report, DE-EE0009664 Figure 37.
